note: Nucleus residency under the resident-service model (architecture 36.2, 36.5, 36.24 step 2). One entry per kernel object linked into the production image (the objects of linker/zephyr80.lk); tools/mapcheck.py fails the build when an object is missing or when a fixed-required object is compiled into the cold areas. Tiers: fixed-required = code that executes, or data that is touched, while the window shows another bank (36.5) - it must link inside 2000h-5FFFh; cold = everything else that belongs to bank 7 (syscall side, boot, loader, extended memory); moves = objects that leave bank 7 for bank 6 in the named stage. Placement in this package: cold objects fill the cold half (6000h-DFFFh); the moves objects that do not fit beside the driver arena overflow into the fixed core's leftover space and are reported as the fixed ledger's overflow. No image sets P outside mode 00 in this package, so every image behaves as at M9.

tiers.fixed-required: Must be visible in the 2000h-5FFFh fixed core: the gates and transition code, the copy primitives, the IRQ executive, the ROMFS bootstrap reader, the processes' raw entry, common-resident boot/panic code and the stacks. mapcheck rejects a fixed-required object whose bytes link at or above 6000h.
tiers.cold: Belongs to bank 7's cold half (6000h-DFFFh), reached only while the window shows bank 7 (P = 0): the syscall dispatcher and bodies, boot and idle, process management, the loader, the device registry and the FS front end.
tiers.moves: Leaves bank 7 for bank 6 in the named stage. Until it leaves it is placed where the cold half's remaining space allows and otherwise overflows into the fixed core's leftover space (reported, not a failure).

objects.reason: zero-byte ABS bound labels describing the driver arena, which lives in the cold half; the object emits no linked bytes and is declared ABS-only, so the build compiles it nowhere (it stays out of cold_half so the residency-driven codegen flags cannot propagate down its dependency on the generated geometry include)
common-resident latch and mode gates: the only mapping-changing code, always visible
diagnostic syscall bodies, reached only through the syscall dispatcher, which the gate runs with P = 0
diagnostic port primitives reached only from the diagnostic syscall bodies (P = 0)
common-resident early console and panic path: must survive any mapping
native FS_* syscall front end, called only from the dispatcher (P = 0); retired in stage 5, when the VFS service and IPC dispatch replace it
IRQ registry and dispatch: the executive runs while the window shows the owner's bank (service-owned IRQs), so its code and data stay visible
linked end of the fixed _CODE area and the SDCC IY trampoline used by the IRQ path
common-resident IRQ stubs and gate; it carries the relocated ISR stack (5F00h-6000h) in its own ABS area
CTC quiesce source driver, called by the dispatcher while the owner's window is open
IM2 vector page in common memory: fetched with whatever mapping is active
kernel boot and idle path: every service-facing call returns with the caller's latch restored, so it only ever runs with P = 0
ZEX/ZMOD loader; its service reads (the executable stream) go through a fixed upcall shim, so the loader body is cold
relocator called by the loader inside the same cold path
string helpers called by the fixed ROMFS bootstrap reader while the window may show another bank
page-zero RST 30h material: must be present in every mode
common-resident panic path: must survive any mapping
IRQ platform bring-up (IM2 vector page, interrupt mode): common-resident
process lifecycle; the exit notification is a nucleus -> VFS upcall through a fixed shim, so the body is cold
exec/exit and the continuation stack; the executable-stream read is a nucleus -> VFS upcall through a fixed shim
common-resident raw application entry jump: no window-visible state
device registry (boot registration and syscall-side lookups, P = 0); retired in stage 4, replaced by the endpoint table
ROM-resident page-zero reset copier: runs before any mapping exists
common-resident ROM-read stub mirrored into every ROM page (mode 00)
the one ROMFS reader, kept in the nucleus as the bootstrap-reader primitive a bank-6 provider calls through the fixed core

VFS core: the ROMFS provider callbacks; package 41 compiles it into the cold half beside the service loader (the drivers left the arena), so the placement is production's own, not the moves tier's fallback
SDCC runtime helpers called from fixed code and from IRQ handlers
common-resident boot entry and C runtime init: runs before the window exists
syscall dispatcher and its bodies: the syscall gate clears the page field before dispatching, so this object only ever runs with P = 0
the syscall transition gate is common-resident by contract (always visible); it saves the caller's whole latch, dispatches with P = 0 and restores exactly
common-resident application-bank copy gate (mode-10 crossings from common memory)

revision-13 upcall shim: cold code that calls a resident service saves the latch, selects the window page, calls and restores; its code, its continuation and its request state must stay visible while the window shows another bank (36.5)
VFS core: directory iteration; package 41 compiles it into the cold half beside the service loader (the drivers left the arena), so the placement is production's own, not the moves tier's fallback
VFS core: file objects move to the VFS service in bank 6
VFS core: mount registry moves to the VFS service in bank 6
VFS core: generated mount table moves to the VFS service in bank 6
VFS core: writable-provider mutations move to the VFS service in bank 6
VFS core: path walking moves to the VFS service in bank 6
VFS core: per-process handles and workspace move to the VFS service in bank 6
VFS core: per-process workspace data moves to the VFS service in bank 6

M10 stage 3 IPC substrate (architecture 36.5, 36.7-36.10): the endpoint table, register/lookup/call, the frame array, the descriptor table and the copy resolvers execute, and are touched, while the window shows bank 6, so they must link inside 2000h-5FFFh.  Linked by the ipc-selftest acceptance image now (test_link); production adopts it in package 41, when the arena drivers leave bank 7.

M10 stage 3 fixed-core IPC primitives (kernel/ipc/ipc_asm.asm): the latch save/select/restore, the window LDIR and the service-stack switch, plus the ABS declaration of the 512-byte service stack at ZOS_SERVICE_STACK_BASE.  Same stage as `ipc`: test images only until package 41.

M10 stage 3 common-resident aperture copy (kernel/ipc/ipc_common.asm, work package 39 correction 01): the path-B primitive runs with mode 10 and page 1 in force, where bank 7 is not mapped, so its code, its request block, its saved latch/SP and its interrupt-push stack must all be common.  It is the only code the fixed-core reservoir of ZOS_COMMON_M10_RESERVATION was held back for.  Same stage as `ipc`: test images only until package 41.

M10 stage 3 IPC syscall bodies (SYS_IPC_LOOKUP / SYS_IPC_CALL, kernel/syscall/ipc.c): reached only through the P-normalizing syscall gate, so they run with the window showing bank 7.  Only the ipc-selftest image links them until package 41.

M10 stage 4 resident-service loader (kernel/service/service_loader.c, architecture 36.11/36.12): reads the boot manifest through the fixed ROMFS reader, validates and places every service image through the common application-bank copy gate, and runs the boot segments and hot inits.  It runs with P = 0 only (the syscall gate normalizes before any syscall, and the boot path is mode 11), so the body is cold code; the acceptance image links it now, production adopts it in package 41.

M10 stage 4 service boot gate (kernel/service/service_boot.asm): switches mode 10 over bank 6 (Q = 6) and calls a boot segment.  Its code and continuation execute with bank 7 unmapped, so the gate is common-resident; its request/transition state is fixed-core data because the upcall shim reads the loader's request block with bank 7 mapped.  Same stage as the loader: test images only until package 41.

IOC class publication for a bank-7 module (kernel/module/ioc_shim.c): it runs in the loader's own phase and is reached from a module's class query, so it lives beside the loader in the cold half and disappears with the IOC-FAT module in package 42

cold_half_note: The production build compiles these objects into the cold areas (_WINDOW / _WINDOW_DATA at 6000h-DFFFh): every cold object, the two IPC cold bodies (the syscall IPC dispatcher and the resident service loader), the IOC class shim the loader publishes to bank-7 modules, and the service-destined VFS objects that fit beside them.  Package 41 moved the drivers out of the arena, so the freed cold space holds what used to overflow into the fixed core, which then holds the substrate; tools/mapcheck.py fails the build when the linked cold code or data overruns the derived bases.  The fixed ledger reports what still overflows.
test_link_note: Empty from package 41 on: production links the IPC substrate (kernel/ipc), the syscall IPC bodies and the resident service loader, so every classified object is a production object again.  The tier classification is the whole rule; the acceptance images add their own test-linked objects, which mapcheck.py reports as fixed-core overflow unless the image places them in the cold half with --cold-extra.
